messages.subject_clean: [aroma.affymetrix] Non-positive probe signals after calibration/normalization (Was: Re: Some questions about plotting and normalization)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeremy.

On 9/2/07, Jeremy Silver <sil...@wehi.edu.au> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> I've been successfully running the allelic cross-talk calibration,
> however it returns negative estimates of probe signals in a
> substantial proportion of probes (~10% in the example I was looking
> at). The log-additive model of RMA can't deal with negative intensity
> estimates. In all your examples (except the one illustrating MbeiPlm),
> you've used RMA as the probe-summarization method.

Yes, you/we should indeed expect non-positive (non-negative + zero)
signals when we calibrate from allelic crosstalk.  In the perfect
world without noise, the calibrated PMB signals of truly AA SNPs
should be all zero, and vice versa for BB SNPs.  With symmetric noise,
it is not surprising that we get both positive and negative signals in
the end.

Yes, the log-additive model is not ideal for non-positive signals
since they all become non-defined (missing values) on the log scale.
Here is when total-copy number analysis comes to a rescue.  If we only
do total-copy number analysis, we don't care how much A or B we've
got, so we simply sum up the PMA+PMB probe pairs, i.e.

  plm <- RmaCnPlm(cs, combineAlleles=TRUE);

This will solve the problem with non-positive signals that are due to
homozygote SNPs.  Thus, if you sum PM=PMA+PMB (*), you should see that
the fraction of non-positive signals goes down substantially.

However, even after summing, some of the PMs (*) may still be
non-positive.  In the perfect world without noise, this only makes
sense if there is no DNA target for that SNP.  We know this is the
case when the true copy-number is zero.  It may also be the case for
mis-annotated probes.  For all other cases, the only rational is that
there is noise added (and/or that the offset estimate in the allelic
calibration is non-perfect).

So, how do we deal with remaining non-positive PMs (*)?  One way to
handle those is simply to discard them *across all chips* like they
never existed, and hope there are enough of positive probes in the
probe set to fit the model.  This chance for this "hope" to be true,
increases if we don't stratify by strand, but fit sense and anti-sense
probes together.  That is, now we've got:

  plm <- RmaCnPlm(cs, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE);
  plm$treatNAsAs <- "NA";

The last line (non-documented) tells aroma.affymetrix to exclude a
probe across arrays if one or more of them are missing (after the log
transform).  So, instead of looking at the fraction of non-positive
probe signals, see how many of your units contain all non-positive
signals (for which we then would get non-defined chip effect
estimates).  Typically this fraction is much smaller.

Even better though, is to only discard single probes, not across
chips.  In order to do this, we can estimate the log-additive model
using a weighted approach where we give weights to each data point
(probe).  We give all non-positive data points zero weight and all
other equal weight.  Ben Bolstad was kind enough to add support for
weights to 'affyPLM' some time ago.  Potentially weights can be used
in other ways too, e.g. spatial quality scores etc.  Here is how you
fit the log-additive model with non-positive probe signals given
weight zero:

  plm <- RmaCnPlm(cs, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE, tags=c("*", "w"));
  plm$treatNAsAs <- "weighted";

Eventually this will be the default settings, but until I've had time
to test it thoroughly (I've used it for a long time, but it should
still be validated, benchmarked etc.).  The tag "*" expands to the
default for the model class and the give arguments; in this case we
get "RMA,A+B,w".

Ok, what about those units/probe sets for which all probes are
non-positive?  This is trickier.  It comes down to several things.
Could they be true zeros, which we cannot model with a log-additive
model anyway, i.e. is the problem due to an invalid model instead of
due to how you calibrated?  If you think you correct for too much
offset in the calibration, or you for other reason accept having a bit
of positive offset in you PM (*) signals, you can shift the signals
before fitting the model using a global constant.  You can do this as:

  plm <- RmaCnPlm(cs, mergeStrands=TRUE, combineAlleles=TRUE,

tags=c("+300", "*", "w"));
  plm$treatNAsAs <- "weighted";
  plm$shift <- +300;

You can always set a shift that makes all your PMs (*) become
positive.  This is indeed what most scanner companies, including
Affymetrix, do to the signals you observe in the first place.

The more shift you add the more bias you will get in you raw CNs,
especially for those in the lower intensity range.

>
> If we apply the cross-talk calibration, should we also use MBEI to get
> probe-level summaries (since it can handle negative intensity
> estimates)? I'm guessing that CRMA, when released will deal with this
> - so I suppose that this is an interim question.

Yes, the multiplicative model (MbeiModel) handles non-positive signals
much better than the log-additive.  Under certain assumptions about
the error terms the two models are actually identical.  However, we've
done ROC evaluations using either model, and the log-additive model
comes out better.  However 2, this might be due to a non-optimal
implementation of the multiplicative model, and not due to a weaker
model.  It has a lot to do with how you robustify the algorithm and
how you deal with heteroscedasticy.  Much more effort for dealing with
this has been put into the log-additive model (affyPLM) compare with
the multiplicative model (affy::fit.li.wong).

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.6.1 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi, aroma.affymetrix v0.6.1 is available.  It mainly address some bugs
in background correction methods, bugs that were introduced in the
latest version of the package.  In addition, the CBS segmentation
method should now be supported.  Here are the details.

Version: 0.6.1 [2007-09-05]
o Added support for fitting copy-number regions using the (fast)
  Circular Binary Segmentation (CBS) method of Venkatraman et al. (2007).
  The method is implemented by the new CbsModel class.  Consider this
  class to be very much in a beta version.
o Added super class CopyNumberSegmentationModel, which provides most of
  the framework to fit and plot segmentation models. By subclassing
  this class, new segmentation methods can be added. Current subclasses
  are GladModel and CbsModel.  ChromosomeExplorer was updated to handle
  multiple segmentation methods.
o Now the startup message when loading the package is generated with
  packageStartupMessage() so that it can be suppressed.
o Put more effort in generating more consistent hash codes that becomes
  part of the filenames of the averaged files.  This modification is
  likely to lead to new hashcodes, and there for new filenames such
  that aroma.affymetrix will not detect existing "average" files.
  In turn, this will mean that stored results from GladModel will
  not be recognized (unless you rename files with the new hashcodes).
o Added a "patch" to make sure that there is rowMedians() supporting
  missing values by looking for the correct version of Biobase,
  R.native or just an apply() notes.  This does unfortunately mean
  that generated hashcodes my be different so certain average CEL
  files will be recalculated, and in turn segmentation results will
  be regenerated.
o PACKAGE DEPENDENCIES: Made R.native an "Supports" package, since it
  is only used for rowMedians() in case the right Biobase version is
  not availble.  R.native is now optional.
o CLEAN UP: Deleted obsolete /inst/chromosomeExplorer/ from source.
o CLEAN UP: Removed some obsolete affxparser patches.
o BUG FIX: getAverageFile() of AffymetrixCelSet had 'na.rm=FALSE'
  by default, which caused a lot of missing values in the average.
  In turn, this cause for instance raw CNs to become missing values.
o BUG FIX: When calling process() on a GcRmaBackgroundCorrection,
  an exception would be thrown with "bgAdjustGcrma() is deprecated.
  Please use the GcRmaBackgroundCorrection class".  The same happend
  with OpticalBackgroundCorrection.  This was due to a typo introduced
  in v0.5.3 when making the underlying functions deprecated.  Thanks
  Jeremy Silver for troubleshooting and reporting this.

See group page for details on how to update/install.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi.

First of all, it is much faster (and much more memory efficient) to
work with binary CDF files rather than ASCII ones, cf. FAQ
(2007-07-09) on the group page.  See same FAQ for instructions how to
convert.  [In a future version, the package might through an error by
default whenever one tries to use an ASCII version.]

I am not sure why RmaBackgroundCorrection would cause R to crash.
Please report sessionInfo() and traceback(), and relevant output from
using verbose output (when calling process()).  However, from previous
experience I would suspect this is related to the CDF file, cf. FAQ
(2007-07-13). Simply retry with the binary CDF and let us know if it
help (repost).  [ A wild guess could be that you are running out of
memory when you try to read from the ASCII CDF which is already 955MB.
 When affxparser/FusionSDK read even a subset of an ASCII CDF, it is
to the best of my understanding that it actually has to read all of
the CDF first, then extract the subset of interest.  On Windows you've
typically only have 2GB/3GB RAM. ]

That you experience summarization to be slow, could, in addition to be
due to an ASCII CDF file, also be (quoting a previous reply) "related
to what Ken noticed for the human exon array where for instance one
unit has ~17000 probes(!), cf.

  http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/optimization-speed-file-space-ram

The fitting time grows exponentially(?) with the number of
probes/chips.  Thus, for such large units alternative
modeling/algorithms have to be found.  I do not know of any work that
attacks this problem.".  Basically, if you only have a few units with
a large number of cells, see if you can avoid fitting those. See the
above URL for how to identify large units.  Let us know if this could
be case and/or if you see a speed up (repost).

For future correspondence, please try to separate different issues in
different message.

Cheers

Henrik

Yes, it looks like the previous problem with R crashing went away when
you converted to a binary CDF.  The problem you've reported below is
unrelated to the RmaBackgroundCorrection class.  I think you get the
same error if you just do:

Correct?  However, I still believe you're running into memory issues
on Windows, that is, that you are using up all available memory that a
single R process can allocate (which is typically 2GB RAM or 3GB if
you really know the tricks).  The reason why I believe so is because I
see the output "Failed to read the CDF file.", and I remember I've
seen myself on Windows when I was really pushing the memory limits; at
some stage affxparser/FusionSDK failed to read my CDF which normally
worked fine.  Your CDF got 2,439,101 units, which is the biggest
number I've seen this far (I've done 1.8*10^6 units myself on
Windows).  BTW, is this a tiling array? FYI, I don't know of anyone
that used aroma.affymetrix for tiling arrays, but someone has to be
the first, ehe ;)

Is there anyway you can make the CDF file available to me so I can try
it out on my Windows machine?  Is it downloadable from somewhere?  If
you make it available to me, could you please make sure to zip/gzip it
first (that would bring it down to ~200-250MB).  You may forward me
the URL offline if you wish too.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.6.2 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi, aroma.affymetrix v0.6.2 is available.  No bug fixes this time;
I'll let the below HISTORY speak for itself:

Version: 0.6.2 [2007-09-07]
o Now setCdf() of AffymetrixCelSet throws an (informative) error message
 whenever one tries to use an ASCII CDF file. This behavior can be
 changed by setting rule 'aroma.affymetrix.settings$rules$allowAsciiCdfs'
 to TRUE in the options. The reason is that working with ASCII CDF files
 is extremely slow and memory inefficient. Use affxparser::convertCdf()
 to convert a CDF into a binary format.
o Updated AllelicCrosstalkCalibration internally.  It now also stores
 the model parameter estimates to file (using a plain save() file format).
o MEMORY OPTIMIZATION: Instead of doing unlist(getCellIndices(cdf, ...),
 use.names=FALSE), we can now do getCellIndices(cdf, useNames=FALSE,
 unlist=TRUE), which is much more memory efficient, e.g. for the
 GenomeWideSNP_6 chip the former uses 25x more memory, which means
 that instead of using 1.4GB we can get away with 60MB.
o CLEAN UP: All calibrateAllelicCrosstalk() methods are now removed.
 Use the AllelicCrosstalkCalibration class instead.
o Package passes R CMD check on R v2.5.1 and R v2.6.0 devel on Windows.
 All redundancy tests works on Linux.

See group page for details on how to update/install.

Cheers

Henrik

  extension (*.CEL).  The main reason for this is that some other
  software don't recognize CEL files with lower-case extension (*.cel).
  Existing CEL files that are in lower case (*.cel) and that are
  generated by the package are renamed to upper case (*.CEL).
  Same thing for generated CDF files.

This is probably why you get the error.  I'll include you bug fix.
Thanks.  You could also solve it by renaming all your *.cel files to
*.CEL files.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

you're heading into non-supported and non-standardized regions here.
This is how you may proceed:

1) Create a tab-delimited file with "genome information", containing
headers "Probe Set ID", "Chromosome", and "Physical Location".  The
file should contain one row per unit, preferably in the order of the
units in the CDF, i.e. first column should pretty much contain the
vector getUnitNames(cdf).  It is important that the first column is
the "Probe Set ID" column.  Use integers for Chromosome (although X
and Y will be translated to 23 and 24, it is better to stick with
numbers because the data can be read much faster).  "Physical
Location" should be the location in bases (not in Mb, not in kb, but
bases).  If the columns are named slightly different, it is possible
to tell aroma.affymetrix to rename them internally, so no worries.
Your file may contain additional column as well.  But if you start
from scratch, it is better to stick with the above.

Name this file <chip type>,genome,<extra tags>.txt.  Put in your
annotationData/chipTypes/<chip type>/ directory.

Make sure you can read it using the following:

# Define a new class
setConstructorS3("MyGenomeInformation", function(...) {
  extend(GenomeInformation(...), "MyGenomeInformation")
})

setMethodS3("readData", "MyGenomeInformation", function(this, ...) {
   readTableInternal(this, ...)
})

# Setup
path <- "annotationData/chipTypes/PFSANGERb520296";
filename <- "PFSANGERb520296,genome,hg18.txt";
gi <- MyGenomeInformation(filename, path=path)

# Make sure the chip type can be inferred from the path
print(getChipType(gi))
# ...or simply

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.7.0 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi, aroma.affymetrix v0.7.0 is available.  It addresses recent
problems discussed on the mailing list and more.  Here are the
details:

Version: 0.7.0 [2007-09-15]
o Now it is possible to specify the genome used for segmentation and
  plotting. This can be done either via argument 'genome' in the
  constructor or by setGenome() of CopyNumberSegmentationModel.
  A corresponding <genome>(,<tags>)*,chromosomes.txt file should be
  put in annotationData/genomes/<genome>/. If not found there, the
  file is searched for in the annotationData/ directory installed
  with the package. If the file is not found, setGenome() will give
  an error.  If not specified, the genome defaults to "Human".
  The above file specifies the number of bases per chromosome,
  which is used when plotting chromosomal data.  The previous file
  'hgChromosomes.txt' is now deprecated and obsolete.
o Now CopyNumberSegmentationModel only adds cytobands to genomes
  for which cytoband information is available.  Currently this is
  hardwired only the "Human" genome. For all other genomes, there
  will be no cytoband.
o Now AllelicCrosstalkCalibration corrects also non-SNP PM cells by
  substracting a global offset and rescaling towards target average.
  The global offset is calculated as the weighted average of all
  allelic offsets. SNP probes are calibrated in the same way as before.
o Updated all places with SNP regular expression "^SNP" to "SNP_" in
  order to also match units named "AFFX-SNP_...".
o SPEED UP: Now getCellMap() of ChipEffectFile caches (large) results
  to file.
o SPEED UP: Now getOutputDataSet() of FragmentLengthNormalization set
  and pass down 'mergeStrands' and 'combineAlleles' to ditto of the
  super class, if applicable.  This way we avoid having to infer those
  arguments from the contents of the files.  This gives an significant
  speed up for large chip types.
o ROBUSTNESS: Now the RmaPlm fit function detects cases where a probe
  get zero weight for all arrays. In such (rare) cases, parameter
  estimates equals NAs. Before an LAPACK error was thrown.
o ROBUSTNESS: Added validate that the 'name' of an AffymetrixCelSet
  and AffymetrixCelFile is of at least length one.
o ROBUSTNESS: Now isDone() of Transform throws an error if too many
  output files are found. Before it used to return FALSE.
o WORKAROUND: If there is only one probe, then fit function of AvgPlm
  would return theta=y:s, and sdTheta=0:s.  However, when searching
  for units to do, we test (sdTheta <= 0).  The workaround is to store
  the smallest float available instead of zero.
o BETA: Added GenericDataFile, GenericDataFileSet, and GenericTabularFile.
o BETA: Added AffymetrixTabularFile, AffymetrixNetAffxCsvFile,
  AromaUgpFile, and AromaUflFile.
o BETA: Added UflSnpInformation and UgpGenomeInformation
  interfacing to UGP and UFL files.
o BETA: Added AvgPlm, AvgSnpPlm, AvgCnPlm.
o BUG FIX: Now more effort is made to ensure that all CEL files are
  generated with an upper-case filename extension (*.CEL) and not (*.cel).
  Thanks Jeremy Silver for reporting problems on this.
o Package passes R CMD check on R v2.5.1pat & R v2.6.0alpha on Windows XP.
  It also passes all redundancy tests on Linux.

See group page for details on how to update/install.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] chromosome display problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi again,

instead of looking for the (almost) hardwired hgChromosomes.txt,  the
new version of aroma.affymetrix will now look for:

  annotationData/genomes/<genome>/<genome>(,<tag>)*,chromosomes.txt

For example:

  annotationData/genomes/Human/Human,chromosomes.txt

Replace "Human" with whatever your genome is.  The file format is the
same as hgChromosomes.txt with all but the 'chromosome' and
'nbrOfBases' columns being options.    The default file for the Human
genome is here:

pathname <- system.file("annotationData/genomes/Human/Human,chromosomes.txt",
package="aroma.affymetrix")

You specify the type of genome, that is, the '<genome>' name above,
via the 'genome' argument to GladModel() or CbsModel(), or
alternatively use setGenome(glad, "<genome>") afterwards.  Then when
plotting, aroma.affymetrix will locate and make use of your file
automatically.

Finally, the generated chromosomal graphs will only include a cytoband
if it is a Human genome, otherwise it will be blank (support for other
genomes might be added, but that is not any of my top priorities).

About the plots not being correct: I suspect that the chromosomal
positional are somehow not read correctly (e.g. it might grab your
'probeScore' column instead of 'physicalPosition'); you'll know that
by using and testing the UGP setup I described in my other reply.

Hope this helps

Henrik

messages.body_plain:
Hi. That good news.

There should be no need for hacks, and aroma.affymetrix should be able
to find your "chromosomes" file that is specific to your genome.  I'm
not sure from you description exactly what you tried.  You should not
have to write/copy anything into the directory where the
aroma.affymetrix package is installed (consider that a read-only area
which will be overwritten next time the package is updated).  Instead
it should go into annotationData/genomes/ in the current directory.
Here is a simple example that illustrate where and how the file should
go, and allows you to test when it works:

library(aroma.affymetrix)

# Pathname of an existing file
src <- system.file("annotationData/genomes/Human/Human,chromosomes.txt",
package="aroma.affymetrix");

# Create a renamed copy of if
path <- "annotationData/genomes/MyOrganism";
mkdirs(path);
pathname <- file.path(path, "MyOrganism,chromosomes.txt");
dest <- file.path(path, "MyOrganism,chromosomes.txt");
file.copy(src, dest);
stopifnot(isFile(dest));

# Create a dummy GLAD model
glad <- GladModel()
# Tell it to use the 'MyOrganism' genome
setGenome(glad, "MyOrganism")
# Ask it to locate the "chromosome" file
pathname2 <- getGenomeFile(glad);
stopifnot(pathname == pathname2);

Let us know when it works - if there is a bug we'll fix it.

Cheers

Henrik

messages.subject: aroma.affymetrix v0.7.1 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi, aroma.affymetrix v0.7.0 is available.

It should fix the recent compatibility problem with
affyPLM/preprocessCore that happens if you are using R v2.6.0 and the
Bioconductor developers version.  I haven't been able to test it
thoroughly across platforms and version because right now I've only
got an easy access to R v2.6.0 on Windows, but the fix is not that
hard so I expect it to work everywhere and to be backward compatible.

Again, please prepare to move to R v2.6.0.  The beta version just got
out, and the release version is planned for October 3.  As soon as the
release version of R v2.6.0 is available, I will stop trying to keep
the code backward compatible with R v2.5.x (there has been too many
changes making this tricky).

Here are the other updates:

Version: 0.7.1 [2007-09-18]
o Now fit() of CopyNumberSegmentationModel reports timing
  information for each chromosome fitted when in verbose mode.
o Now importFromAffymetrixNetAffxCsvFile() of AromaUgpFile averages
  positions if multiple positions were available for a particular unit.
o ROBUSTNESS: Made createFrom() of AffymetrixCelFile fail safe,
  that is, the destination file will not be created unless it
  is complete.  This is done by first create/writing to a temporary
  file which is then renamed at the end. This should minimize the
  risk of creating incomplete CEL files.
o ROBUSTNESS: Added internal fileCopy() which copies a file via
  a temporary file which is renamed.  All file copying in the
  package is now done via this method.
o CLEAN UP: Removed obsolete copyFile() from AffymetrixFile in
  favor of copyTo() in GenericDataFile.
o BETA: Added trial version of ScaleNormalization.
o BUG FIX: Due to a migration of code from affyPLM to preprocessCore,
  the fit function returned by getFitFunction() would not work with
  affyPLM >= 1.13.9.  Now getFitFunction() adopts to the version of
  affyPLM/preprocessCore installed.  If preprocessCore v0.99.16 or
  newer is available, that is used, otherwise affyPLM v1.13.8 or older
  is used. This has been veried to work on i) R v2.5.1pat with
  affyPLM v1.12.0, and R v2.6.0alpha with preprocessCode v0.99.16.
  (affyPLM v1.13.6).
o BUG FIX: The workaround storing single-probe sdTheta estimates
  as a small value was set for single-*chip* not probe cases.
o BUG FIX: getFragmentLengths() of UflSnpInformation would thrown
  an error "Unknown fields: fragmentLength".  Now getDataColumns()
  returns the correct names.

See group page for details on how to update/install.

Cheers

Henrik

Hi,

if you're working with exon arrays, a patch for ExonRmaPlm is
available that addresses the recent affyPLM/preprocessCore version
issues.  Just do the following once, and it will be applied whenever
you load the package and until the next version is released:

library(aroma.affymetrix)
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")

Cheers

Henrik
